name: Curiosity
definition: You learn rapidly and eagerly; you are as interested in other people's ideas as your own; you're humble about what you don't yet know.

rows.situation: Work that needs something you do not know yet
rows.under: Fakes fluency, or waits for someone else to learn it.
rows.justRight: Learns the missing piece fast enough to use it, and says what you still do not know.
rows.over: Goes deep on the interesting adjacent topic and does not come back to the work.

rows.situation: A colleague's idea that competes with yours
rows.under: Listens only long enough to answer it.
rows.justRight: Gets interested in it. Asks the question that would make it better, whether or not you adopt it.
rows.over: Abandons your own prepared view at the first interesting alternative.

rows.situation: A domain you are new to
rows.under: Speaks as if tenure elsewhere transfers.
rows.justRight: Asks the basic questions early, and uses the answers.
rows.over: Stays in student mode after you know enough to decide, and the team carries you.

rows.under: Files it as bad luck and moves on.
rows.justRight: Finds out why you were surprised and changes the next attempt.
rows.over: Turns the postmortem into a seminar and the next attempt never starts.

rows.situation: A question you would love to chase while a commitment is open
rows.under: Refuses every question that was not on Monday's list, including the one that would have saved the work.
rows.justRight: Writes the question down, finishes the commitment, and comes back if the question still matters.
rows.over: Chases it and lets the commitment slip without a word.
